extracted.intended_audience: business executives, corporate public-relations counselors, and PR practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and executing corporate public-relations campaigns and ongoing public-relationship policies so as to build goodwill, influence public opinion, and align business objectives with public interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use influential leaders and staged events
rubrics_metrics.description: To this ceremony key people, persons known to influence the buying habits of the public, such as a famous violinist, a popular artist, and a society leader, are invited. These key persons affect other groups, lifting the idea ... and the idea which they are dramatizing, are then projected to the wider public through various publicity channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage events or ceremonies that include respected/visible leaders to lend prestige and create associative transfer; invite artists, society leaders, or other opinion leaders; publicize the event broadly so the leaders' endorsement is amplified; use leading architects/decorators so others imitate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create associative environments to induce self-motivated purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: The music room will be accepted because it has been made the thing. And the man or woman who has a music room ... will naturally think of buying a piano. It will come to him as his own idea. Under the old salesmanship the manufacturer said to the prospective purchaser, 'Please buy a piano.' The new salesmanship has reversed the process and caused the prospective purchaser to say to the manufacturer, 'Please sell me a piano.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design environments, architectural features, exhibits and symbolic settings that associate the product with desirable lifestyles so consumers internalize the idea and ask for the product themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilize group formation and competitions to spread ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the most effective methods is the utilization of the group formation of modern society ... nationwide competitions for sculpture in Ivory soap, open to school children ... The best pieces are selected from the local competitions for entry in the national contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create contests and group activities (school competitions, local-to-national progression) that engage social groups, scale participation, and enlist institutions (schools, art centers) to distribute and legitimize the campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activate multiple psychological motives
rubrics_metrics.description: A number of familiar psychological motives were set in motion in the carrying out of this campaign. The esthetic, the competitive, the gregarious ... the snobbish ... the exhibitionist, and ... the maternal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design campaigns that simultaneously appeal to varied motives (aesthetic pride, competition, social belonging, status imitation, exhibition, parental instincts) to multiply participation and goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align campaign with leaders' and stakeholders' interests (disinterested aspect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The leaders who lend their authority to any propaganda campaign will do so only if it can be made to touch their own interests. There must be a disinterested aspect of the propagandist’s activities. In other words, it is one of the functions of the public relations counsel to discover at what points his client’s interests coincide with those of other individuals or groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discover and emphasize overlapping interests so third-party leaders or institutions will lend authority; craft initiatives that serve both the sponsor and the endorsers' genuine interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue mutual-interest community activities (enlightened self-interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: The company then establishes relations with chambers of commerce ... It helps them to secure new plants and industries for the town. It facilitates business through the dissemination of technical information. ... A bank institutes an investment service for the benefit of its customers ... a baking company establishes an information service suggesting recipes for bread ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop services/programs that genuinely benefit communities or customers (investment services, insurance, educational materials) so they both serve the public good and create business benefits—enlightened self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the public's structure, prejudices, and whims; do not run counter to them
rubrics_metrics.description: The man in charge of a firm’s public relations must be familiar with the structure, the prejudices, and the whims of the general public, and must handle his problems with the utmost care. The public has its own standards and demands and habits. You may modify them, but you dare not run counter to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct research into public attitudes; avoid campaigns that directly oppose entrenched public norms; use leaders and indirect approaches to achieve change gradually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatize and interpret company personality consistently across touchpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Business must express itself and its entire corporate existence so that the public will understand and accept it. It must dramatize its personality ... A store specializing in fashionable men’s clothing will express in its architecture the authenticity of the goods it offers. ... it may be as important that the doorman be polite, or that the floors be kept clean, as that the branch manager be an able financier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure architecture, displays, staff behavior, packaging, advertising and social activities all convey a coherent, authentic corporate persona aligned with objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid false impressions; practice truthful public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations activities of a business cannot be a protective coloring to hide its real aims. It is bad business as well as bad morals to feature exclusively a few high-class articles, when the main stock is of medium grade or cheap ... A sound public relations policy will not attempt to stampede the public with exaggerated claims and false pretenses, but to interpret the individual business vividly and truly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be truthful and avoid exaggeration or deceptive 'window-dressing'; long-term reputation depends on authentic representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose between continuous interpretation and high-spotting
rubrics_metrics.description: His general plan of work may be reduced to two types, which I might term continuous interpretation and dramatization by high-spotting. Continuous interpretation is achieved by trying to control every approach to the public mind ... High-spotting, on the other hand, vividly seizes the attention of the public and fixes it upon some detail ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether to pursue subtle, pervasive messaging across many touchpoints (continuous interpretation) or concentrated dramatic stunts/events (high-spotting), or a combination, after studying objectives and possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scientific tests and pilot implementations to build credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The advantages in increasing the digestibility and nutritional value of milk were proven in the Mellon Institute of Industrial Research. The suggestion was made ... that gelatine be used by certain hospitals and school systems, to be tested out there. The favorable results ... were then projected to other leaders in the field ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission credible scientific research or pilot programs (institutes, hospitals, schools) and publicize favorable results via expert channels to build authoritative acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and respond to public opinion trends; survey and advise policy modification
rubrics_metrics.description: The public relations counsel should anticipate such trends of public opinion and advise on how to avert them, either by convincing the public that its fears ... are unjustified, or in certain cases by modifying the action of the client to the extent necessary to remove the cause of complaint. ... public opinion might be surveyed and the points of irreducible opposition discovered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor opinion, run surveys to identify entrenched opposition vs explainable concerns, and recommend either persuasive messaging or concrete policy changes to address causes of complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address responsibilities to multiple stakeholder groups and tailor communications
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a responsibility to the stockholders ... toward the dealer ... toward the industry as a whole ... toward the retailer ... toward the consumer ... And the general public ... There is no detail too trivial to influence the public in a favorable or unfavorable sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify key stakeholders (stockholders, dealers, retailers, consumers, general public) and use tailored channels (letters, factory visits, inspections, dealer relations) appropriate to each group's needs and influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create value-added services/institutions to promote product use and public welfare
rubrics_metrics.description: He organized, as part of his business, a foot protection bureau. This bureau disseminated scientifically accurate information on the proper care of the feet, principles which the manufacturer had incorporated in the construction of the shoes. The result was that civic bodies, police chiefs ... furthered the ideas his product stood for and the product itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish bureaus, information services, insurance departments, or other institutional offerings that educate or protect customers and thereby promote product adoption and public benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage credible third-party institutions and authorities for legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The contest was held under the auspices of the Art Center in New York City, an organization of high standing in the art world. ... distinguished judges, establishes the contest as a serious art event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partner with respected institutions (art centers, universities, hospitals, research institutes) or prominent judges/experts to lend prestige and remove perceptions of mere commercial self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amplify events and associations through publicity channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The juxtaposition of these leaders, and the idea which they are dramatizing, are then projected to the wider public through various publicity channels. ... made cognizant of it through newspaper and magazine and other publicity, with the effect of building up definitely the prestige of the development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use newspapers, magazines and mass publicity to project staged events, competitions, and leader endorsements to a wide audience to maximize reputational effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counter unethical or exaggerated advertising by using expert and institutional channels
rubrics_metrics.description: The competing manufacturer is put in the position either of overemphasizing ... He turns to the weapon of propaganda which can effectively, through various channels of approach to the public—the dental clinics, the schools, the women’s clubs, the medical colleges, the dental press and even the daily press—bring to the public the truth of what a tooth paste can do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When competitors make exaggerated claims, use educational, professional, and institutional channels to present accurate information and protect the honest product's market position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to trivial operational details as part of public relations
rubrics_metrics.description: The modifications then recommended ... may concern the broadest matters of policy or the apparently most trivial details of execution. ... it may be as important that the doorman be polite, or that the floors be kept clean, as that the branch manager be an able financier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and adjust seemingly minor details (clerk dress, doorman politeness, factory cleanliness, window displays) because they materially affect public perception and campaign success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build public acceptance to enable financial operations and international reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Practically all prosperous corporations expect at some time to enlarge operations, and will need to float new stock or bond issues. The success of such issues depends upon the general record of the concern ... The growth of big business is so rapid that in some lines ownership is more international than national. It is necessary to reach ever larger groups of people ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PR to create the public goodwill necessary for successful stock/bond offerings, mergers, and for acceptance in international capital markets; tailor messaging for national or international audiences as required.
